articles.title: Calls of the wild offer sound guidance for protecting animals
articles.snippet: The wild world is full of roars, whoops and songs. Scientists are using such sounds to guide efforts to help save species at threat of extinction.

articles.title: Bees may survive a swim by heading for the dark [COMIC]
articles.snippet: Researchers recently learned that bees can swim. New findings show that bees paddle toward shade and dark to reach shore.

articles.title: Is AI making us dumber? Depends how it’s used
articles.snippet: AI can weaken learning when it replaces effort. But tools that offer guidance rather than answers can help people hone their skills.

articles.title: And the science Nobels for 2026 go to …
articles.snippet: Top prizes went for an icy window into the cosmos, a light switch for the brain and solving the mystery of mirror image molecules.

articles.title: Scientists Say: Theropod
articles.snippet: This group of dinosaurs once included Tyrannosaurus rex . Today, they include birds.

articles.title: Could Spider-Man really turn off his superpowers?
articles.snippet: In Spider-Man: Brand New Day, Peter Parker devises a superpower inhibitor based on real RNA therapies.

articles.title: Anger or fear? Dogs may be able to read it on your face
articles.snippet: Brain scans offer the first evidence that dogs can read certain human facial expressions.

articles.title: These clues might point to life on other worlds
articles.snippet: Gases and color on distant planets may trace to activity by extraterrestrial life. If so, those E.T.s are likely tiny, one-celled beings.

articles.title: Some germs ride a superhighway at the edge of space
articles.snippet: Some microbes common on Earth’s surface lead a secret double life. Soaring higher than jumbo jets, they carry clues about disease spread and alien life.

articles.title: Experiment: Discover the science behind afterimages
articles.snippet: By observing afterimages, you can learn how different cone cells in the retina respond to various colors.

articles.title: Physicists may have finally glimpsed elusive dark matter
articles.snippet: For decades scientists have been trying to detect this invisible substance that fills the cosmos. The LZ experiment may have finally spied it.

articles.title: Let’s learn about origami-inspired science
articles.snippet: The Japanese art of paper folding has inspired new designs for lightweight and shapeshifting technology.
